subject: POC Kickoff & Capacity Planning — Scheduling Hands-on Session
messages:
From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC kickoff — coordinating next steps

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the fast responses last week — we're excited to get the POC started. We'd like to schedule a 90-minute hands-on kickoff the week of Mar 23. High-level agenda: quick intro, walkthrough of Redwood API, prompt review & routing rules, and a short load test to validate token throughput.

Attendees on our side: Jordan Smith (Platform PM), Priya Kapoor (SRE), and Michael Lee (data). Preferred windows: Tue/Wed 9:30–12:00 PT or Thu 13:00–16:00 PT.

Two asks before the kickoff:
- Can you confirm whether the POC will run against Hosted or Dedicated capacity by default?
- We need a rough token budget and any quota bumps required to run a 10k token/hour load test.

Thanks — if you can propose 2–3 slots, we'll confirm with our SRE.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Smith
Platform PM, Acme Corp
Attachment: POC_requirements.docx (see brief)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — coordinating next steps

Hi Jordan — thanks for the timeline and attendee list. We're excited to run this with you.

Quick answers up front:
- Default: we typically run initial POCs on Hosted for fastest time-to-value, but we can spin up a short Dedicated trial if you need guaranteed throughput for load tests.
- Token budget: for a 90-minute session with a short load test (10k token/hour ~ 15k tokens total for the session) we recommend a token budget of 50k to allow for exploratory prompts and retries.

Proposed times (PT):
1) Tue Mar 24, 10:00–11:30
2) Wed Mar 25, 09:30–11:00
3) Thu Mar 26, 13:30–15:00

Dylan (engineer) and Dev (solutions) are looped in for the load test and routing discussion. Dylan — can you confirm what we'll need from their side (test endpoints, dataset, and any expected RPS)? Dev — I'll follow up with a calendar invite and POC scope.

I'll attach the POC scope and a starter capacity plan for your review.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: POC_scope.pdf

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff — coordinating next steps

Thanks Marissa. Jordan — a couple of technical notes to make the session productive:

1) For the load test: if you want to validate 10k tokens/hour sustained we can run that against Hosted with a temporary quota bump; for tight tail-latency SLOs we recommend a short Dedicated trial (2–4 GPUs) for the load phase.

2) Inputs we'll need from you:
- Example prompts (or a small sample dataset) so we can pre-warm KV cache and create routing rules.
- Expected concurrency (RPS) and token distribution (avg tokens per request).

3) I'll bring a quick test harness and a capacity_plan.xlsx that maps tokens/hour -> GPUs/throughput and estimated cost. I'll attach it here for visibility.

If we go Hosted + quota bump, Dev can request the bump (usually 24–48 hrs). If you need Dedicated for the load window, we'll open a short-term Dedicated trial (requires a signed POC addendum).

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: capacity_plan.xlsx (spreadsheet)
